hook: Read this one top to bottom and avoid skipping ahead. It starts as a modest recovered record about a man who cannot be hurt, and the way the document is assembled matters more than it first seems. Small, slightly awkward moments in the interview are worth noticing.
whyItMatters: It is a compact showcase for the meta tag: the anomaly lives in the record as much as in the man, so the reader ends up among the people being misled. A Keter, uncontained file that begins by describing something almost dull makes a strong contrast. It shows how much a short article can achieve by revising its own evidence partway through.
thingsToNotice:
The structure is a before and after. The same interview appears twice, and the second copy restores what was filtered out, while Dr. Loyd's lines stay word for word the same; his polite replies turn chilling once you see what they were answering.

The handwritten note in the middle shows the effect from inside, a staff that gradually stopped questioning its own losses. The subject's despair adds a second layer, since being overlooked is a torment for him as well. Details like the ban on automated systems in the new containment area quietly confirm how far his influence reaches.

related.note: Another anomaly defined by what people fail to register about it.
Pairs well for its play with how the document itself is written.
